content:
Hi all — I've been working on a Lean 4 formalization of the Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic function fields, and it's now at a complete, kernel-checked state. Source (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/vaca22/riemann-roch-function-fields

A few highlights:

  • The public API is coordinate-free: divisors are indexed by intrinsic places (discrete rank-one valuation subrings containing the constants), with an equivalence to a two-chart coordinate model via Ostrowski.
  • riemann_roch, duality (the index of specialty), Clifford's and Riemann's inequalities, and corollaries C1–C6 are all proved; genus, L(D), Weil differentials, and an intrinsic adele space are set up.
  • It's axiom-clean — the headline theorems depend only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] — with zero sorry/admit (there is an AxiomCheck.lean to run).
  • As a worked application, on a Weierstrass elliptic curve it derives genus 1 and the degree-one Picard-torsor / class-group dictionary, compatible with the group law.

It's built against Mathlib v4.31.0. I'm now working on upstreaming the pieces into Mathlib as small, reviewable slices (starting with the Dedekind-domain divisor group). Feedback on the design — especially the place/adele abstractions and how best to align them with existing Mathlib API — would be very welcome.
Congratulations! Note that we basically already have divisors for Dedekind domains, ClassGroup is actually defined as Weil Cartier divisors.
See also #maths > Progress towards Riemann-Roch and #maths > "The" Riemann-Roch theorem

Thanks for the pointer, @Riccardo Brasca — you're right that Mathlib already has count and the factorization API for divisors, so I've closed #41674.

The core of what I've been building isn't the divisor group, though — it's the adelic Riemann–Roch theory for function fields: the spaces L(D), K-valued adeles, Weil differentials, the duality theorem, and the riemann_roch theorem itself. As far as I can tell, Mathlib doesn't have these yet.

I think this is complementary to the scheme-theoretic version @Raphael Douglas Giles is developing in #41621, not a duplicate. And for places, I'd rather build on the existing definitions from @María Inés de Frutos Fernández and @Xavier Généreux than reinvent them.

Two questions for the community:

  1. Is there interest in a Riemann–Roch aimed specifically at the function-field setting?
  2. For the place side, should I build entirely on top of the existing library definitions?
As to 1., my opinion is that we should eventually have both versions of the theory of algebraic curves (via function fields and via schemes), together with the dictionary between them.
